decisions.decision: The board agreed the June 3rd warrant article will ask voters to approve funding for the full project scope (design plus construction) rather than a smaller piece.

The board agreed to keep its existing tiered water rate structure and use the Waterworth billing software to model how the new debt service would be spread across usage tiers before publishing a per-household cost figure.

Agreed that items requiring real discussion should be listed as explicit agenda items rather than under 'additions,' and that draft agendas be circulated to commissioners a few days before the required posting deadline.
Agreed to hold weekly Wednesday meetings leading up to the June 3rd vote, deciding meeting-by-meeting whether each one is needed.

Tabled the question of whether the district should produce its own public-access video in response to a citizens' group's video, pending the superintendent gathering more information from the public access coordinator.
Agreed to place the resident's long-pending agenda item request on next week's meeting agenda.

minutes.headline: Water Commissioners set a June special vote on a large loan to fund PFAS and manganese treatment.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District board spent most of the meeting with its engineer reviewing how State Revolving Fund financing and bidding works for a combined PFAS and iron/manganese treatment project, and finalizing warrant-article language and cost-to-ratepayer estimates ahead of a June 3rd special district meeting where voters will be asked to fund the project. The board also voted to bar equipment access through the water supply protection zone for a tree removal, discussed an unresolved dispute over a kayak rack sited in that same zone, authorized spending on postcards and social media to publicize the June 3rd vote, and heard public comments criticizing the board's conduct during a heated exchange and a resident's request for a long-pending agenda item.

what_happened.line: Water Commissioners set a special district meeting for June 3rd to ask voters to fund PFAS and manganese treatment.
The board agreed the warrant article will cover the full project scope, design and construction together, not a smaller piece.
Commissioners voted to bar all equipment access through the water supply protection zone for a nearby tree removal.
The board authorized spending with a marketing contractor on postcards and social media to publicize the June 3rd vote.
The board agreed to keep the existing tiered water rate structure and model debt service across usage tiers before publishing a cost estimate.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked at the June 3rd special district meeting to approve loan funding for PFAS and iron/manganese treatment, which will show up on water bills through the rate tiers.
A per-household or per-tier cost estimate has not yet been published; the board said it wants that worked out on the district's billing software before the vote.
A separate, unresolved dispute over a kayak rack sited in the same water supply protection zone remains open, with a variance letter to the state whose outcome was not clearly recorded.
